plan: Root cause from evidence: forward and input_grad are pointwise and were bitwise on all 48 actual native replays, all 44 operator cases, 2 guards and 2 offsets; the only association-sensitive op is the per-row weights_grad sum over H. Candidate001 reduced with a flat 1D tl.arange(0,BLOCK) and tl.sum(axis=0); for the actual H=2048 expert at call47/N97 that tree-reduction association rounded one BF16 element to the adjacent value (abs 9.5367431640625e-7), which propagated to the two step-3 embedding gradients that failed full training. Candidate002 fixed numerics via standalone torch.compile but lost the immutable closure reuse and added costly dispatch (fwd+bwd median 0.1533579ms vs 0.1074183ms native). Candidate003 keeps the two verified Triton kernels byte-for-byte and replaces ONLY the wgrad reduction with a plain Triton JIT kernel that copies the ACTUAL original Inductor 2D reduction loop body from original-reduction.py, then restores candidate001's guarded closure cache for all three kernels.

Public entry weighted_swiglu(x, weights, *, native) keeps the exact 001 guard predicate (CUDA, BF16/BF16, x.dim() in (2,3), weights.dim()==2 with last dim 1, both contiguous, even last dim, weights.shape[0]==flattened row count). Any unsupported input (CPU, FP32, non-contiguous, dtype/shape mismatch) delegates the WHOLE function once to native(x, weights) with the exact objects, so CPU and FP32 guard probes see zero native_fallback_calls on supported shapes and no hidden callthrough on supported ones.

Keep forward kernel identical to 001: a,b gate/up and w loaded BF16 then .to(fp32); sig=tl.sigmoid(a); y=((a*sig)*b)*w; single BF16 store over the flat H-sized output grid (BLOCK=1024, num_warps=4). Keep input_grad kernel identical to 001: gg=g*w first; sig=tl.sigmoid(a); tmp8=gg*sig; tmp10=1-sig; tmp11=a*tmp10; tmp12=tmp11+1; tmp13=tmp8*tmp12; dx_gate=tmp13*b; dx_up=gg*(a*tl.sigmoid(a)); two BF16 stores, both halves per program. Both were association-free and bitwise on every replay, so they are retained verbatim.

weights_grad kernel copies the original Inductor triton_red_fused_mul_silu_sum_1 body: XBLOCK=1 (one program per row via grid=(N,1,1)), xindex=pid[:,None], xmask=xindex<xnumel, rbase=tl.arange(0,RBLOCK)[None,:], _tmp=tl.full([XBLOCK,RBLOCK],0,tl.float32); for roffset in range(0,H,RBLOCK): rindex=roffset+rbase, rmask=rindex<H; load gate tmp0=in_ptr0[r1+TWO_H*x0], up tmp5=in_ptr0[H+r1+TWO_H*x0], g tmp7=in_ptr1[r1+H*x0] all masked other=0.0 .to(fp32); tmp1=tmp0.to(fp32); tmp2=sigmoid(tmp1); tmp3=tmp1*tmp2; tmp4=tmp3.to(fp32); tmp6=tmp4*tmp5; tmp8=tmp6*tmp7; tmp9=broadcast_to(tmp8,[XBLOCK,RBLOCK]); _tmp=tl.where(rmask&xmask,_tmp+tmp9,_tmp); then tmp=tl.sum(_tmp,1)[:,None]; store out_ptr0[x0]. This preserves the exact FP32 op order and the [XBLOCK,RBLOCK]->axis=1 sum association before the single BF16 store, instead of 001's flat axis=0 tree.

Generalize H via constexpr H and TWO_H=2*H strides (no hardcoded 4096/2048). RBLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(H) so the loop runs exactly once for every contract width (H=2048->2048 matching the original launcher config, H=769->1024, H=257->512), with rmask=rindex<H zeroing tail lanes; num_warps=8 when RBLOCK>=2048 (actual H=2048) else 4; num_stages=1 always. Masked other=0.0 keeps empty/tail/odd widths safe and within unchanged atol 3e-4 / rtol 1e-3.

torch.autograd.Function saves only (x, weights) and ctx.H. forward allocates a fresh (prefix,H) BF16 out and launches the forward kernel only when out.numel()!=0 (empty returns the empty out, no launch, no divide math). backward calls g=g.contiguous(), allocates fresh dx=empty_like(x) and dw=empty_like(weights) every call; when g.numel()!=0 it launches input_grad then wgrad with N=numel//H; numel==0 returns the fresh empty dx,dw with no launch. Nothing cached is ever an output tensor, pointer or stream.

Restore the guarded CURRENT-ARG immutable CompiledKernel launch closure reuse for ALL three kernels via a shared _launch_cache plus a _state['closure_ok'] flag. Keys are exact per phase: fwd=(phase,device,numel,H,grid,x%16,w%16,out%16); bwd_input=(phase,device,numel,H,grid,x%16,g%16,w%16,dx%16); wgrad=(phase,device,N,H,grid=N,RBLOCK,num_warps,x%16,g%16,dw%16). Hit: call the cached launcher with CURRENT runtime args (constexpr H/TWO_H/XBLOCK/RBLOCK dropped) so fresh tensors and the active stream are used every launch; miss: kernel[grid](args, constexprs..., num_warps, num_stages) launches and compiled[grid] is stored. A first closure-call failure flips closure_ok False, clears the cache, and all later calls take the plain kernel[grid] miss path, so correctness never depends on the closure arity and a re-launch is idempotent.

Imports limited to torch, triton, triton.language; no torch._inductor import, no codecache, no generated .py read, no filesystem/network/process/env/seed/feedback access, and no hardcoded observed values or addresses. The Inductor math is inlined directly (tl.sigmoid, no libdevice/triton_helpers needed). No change to router, GEMMs, dispatch, CE, gradnorm, fusion, model, dtype, optimizer, seed, timing, tolerance or the numerical gate; native/control/optimized keep the same process-only uint8 stable-sort compatibility.

Promotion path unchanged and not pre-judged: candidate003 must independently pass the original probe + 2 actual offset + 48 actual-native replays + 3 training comparisons before any performance claim. Only then fresh full-MoE numerical admission (router probabilities/maps and probability gradients included), control=CE0008+gradnorm001, optimized=control plus only this candidate; 120 steps with first 20 discarded across seeds 34102/34103/34104 on the unchanged native GPU-synchronized timer; promote only if strictly >1% incremental throughput vs same-round control AND faster on all three seeds, else keep native weighted SwiGLU. Hypothesized speed/bitwise parity is treated as unverified until these gates.
risks: Bitwise parity of the wgrad kernel with Inductor now depends on the vendor Triton 2.4.1 compiler lowering the copied [XBLOCK=1,RBLOCK=2048] accumulate + tl.sum(axis=1)[:,None] to the identical FP32 reduction association as the original triton_red_fused_mul_silu_sum_1; if the vendor backend reassociates or inserts an extra cast, the N97 1-ULP divergence that broke 001 could persist and the formal numerical gate may still reject.

RBLOCK=next_power_of_2(H) gives a single loop iteration for every contract width, so the H=2048 association matches the original exactly; for H=257/769 the association is a plausible (not guaranteed) match to whatever Inductor would emit at those widths, relying on the masked other=0.0 and the unchanged tolerance to stay admissible.

Closure arity for the extra runtime xnumel arg (closure(x,w,out,numel) / closure(x,g,w,dx,numel) / closure(x,g,dw,N)) in vendor Triton 2.4.1 is unverified; if the cached launcher rejects these runtime args, closure_ok flips and every launch falls back to the correct-but-slower kernel[grid] path, so the >1% gain gate may not be met even though numerics are unaffected.

data_ptr()%16 plus exact-numel/N keying is conservative: alternating expert token counts (N=38..256) and odd-offset views create many closure classes, which can dilute the cache-hit benefit without harming correctness.

int32 offset arithmetic (TWO_H*x0 up to ~2.1M for N=256,H=2048) is safe for the declared moe-weighted shapes but would overflow for much larger inputs; this candidate targets only the observed contract shapes.

The closures fetch the active stream per launch, matching native; if a harness path pins a stream around the module hook, the two fresh-input non-default-stream probes must be re-confirmed. No tolerance, timing, dtype or baseline-fusion weakening is introduced to compensate.

eviction_policy='evict_first' is copied verbatim from the original body for faithfulness; it is a cache hint with no numerical effect, but if the vendor runtime rejects the kwarg the wgrad kernel would need it removed, which is a lowering-compatibility (not correctness) risk.
